jess: quick sanity check — seeing auth header disappear on 307 redirects in our kotlin client when using an app interceptor + shaded libs. repro: upload streaming request -> server responds 307 -> client follows redirect but Authorization gone. Anyone seen this?

leo: yup, classic. OkHttp drops headers on redirect unless you re-add them. Two quick fixes: 1) use a NetworkInterceptor to mutate the request (keeps headers), or 2) set followRedirects(false) and handle manually keeping Authorization.

maria: also watch out for interceptors order. Application interceptors see the original request before redirects are applied. Network interceptors see the request as it hits the socket. If you need the header preserved across redirects, reapply it in an authenticator or in your redirect-handling code.

jess: thanks. any sample snippet for network interceptor?

leo: sure — small example: ```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .addNetworkInterceptor { chain ->
    val req = chain.request().newBuilder()
      .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${TokenStore.get()}")
      .build()
    chain.proceed(req)
  }
  .followRedirects(true) // still ok
  .build()
```
This will ensure header present on socket-level requests.

sam: I recommend using an Authenticator for 401 refresh flow instead of relying on interceptors for token refresh-on-refresh. Authenticator runs after redirects/authorization failures and can reissue requests with new creds. Also be careful with idempotency — don't automatically retry non-idempotent POSTs.

jess: good point re: authenticator. We're also seeing weird serialization differences between Jackson and Gson when shading both into the client jar (some services use one, some the other). Any best practices?

maria: shading both is dangerous — classloader duplication or relocation mismatches cause runtime surprises. Prefer: a single JSON lib in the standalone client (relocate com.fasterxml.jackson to our package, and relocate com.google.gson similarly) so there are no collisions. Or provide adapters so the SDK only exposes one canonical serialization path.

sam: if you must include both, relocate package names in Gradle (shadowJar) and test the TypeAdapter/Module registries. Example relocate rules: ```gradle
shadowJar {
  relocate 'com.fasterxml.jackson', 'com.redwood.shaded.fasterxml.jackson'
  relocate 'com.google.gson', 'com.redwood.shaded.gson'
}
```
But ensure any reflective access (Jackson afterburner, etc.) still works — you might need to add keep rules.

leo: unrelated but saw NDJSON streaming edge: using `source.readUtf8LineStrict()` can throw if server sends partial chunk and you have timeouts. Prefer consume via bufferedLines or readUtf8() with careful delimiting. Simple pattern: 
```kotlin
val source = response.body!!.source()
while (!source.exhausted()) {
  val line = source.readUtf8Line() ?: break
  if (line.isBlank()) continue
  processJson(line)
}
```
This tolerates partial final chunks better.

jess: thanks — we had a failing production stream where client threw EOFException. switching to readUtf8Line() helped in staging.

build-bot: CI repro attached — failing test: `StreamClientTest#partialChunkHandling` on JDK 17, stack: `java.io.EOFException at okio.RealBufferedSource.readUtf8Line(RealBufferedSource.kt:...)`

maria: also check read timeout vs ping interval on load balancers. LB may drop idle connection which shows as EOF. Add keepalive/ping or shorter readTimeout.

jess: action items: 1) change auth header handling -> move to network interceptor + Authenticator for refresh, 2) update shadowJar relocations and add integration test for jackson/gson shaded, 3) switch streaming parser to tolerant readUtf8Line() and add LB/timeout tests. I'll open a PR. Thanks all :thumbsup:
